payload.summary: Planned the first working disaster-recovery backup scheme for the gx-10 self-hosted migration. Investigation established that the existing pg_cron backup has never produced a backup (MinIO endpoint never wired, job body self-skips, mc binary absent from the DB image), and that its health check is gated behind the railway provider so it cannot fire on gx-10. Selected a Python-orchestrated, native-tool-executing design across seven work packages with no scope or lock overlap.

decisions.title: Host-side only; railway/postgres/** untouched
decisions.rationale: verify-production-paradedb-langfuse edits those files and treats the current backup as a cutover precondition; repointing it mid-flight would invalidate that change's rollback evidence. The dead-job finding is recorded in docs/GOTCHAS.md instead.

decisions.title: RPO 24h via daily dumps; WAL archiving deferred
decisions.rationale: Ingested content is re-derivable from still-available external sources. Human-authored data (review decisions, prompt and source overrides) is the real exposure and is the trigger to revisit. A tested simple restore beats an untested complex one for RTO.

decisions.title: Client-side age encryption before upload
decisions.rationale: Dumps contain subscriber emails, OAuth tokens and audit logs. SSE protects against disk theft but not against bucket-credential holders. Client-side encryption turns a credential leak into a denial-of-access problem.

decisions.title: Freshness derives from a bucket-side manifest, not cron.job_run_details
decisions.rationale: The question that matters is whether an artifact arrived at the destination, not whether the source believes it ran. A manifest answers that, is provider-independent, and survives destruction of the source host.

decisions.title: Widen the durable alert path rather than use in-app notifications
decisions.rationale: The in-app path fails open, so a failed alert is indistinguishable from no problem — unacceptable for a durability signal. Widening WorkflowAlertEnvelopeV1 requires changing five elements together and making operation-scoped fields optional rather than synthesized.

decisions.title: Retention via provider-side lifecycle rules; no unattended delete
decisions.rationale: Provider-side retention keeps working while gx-10 is down — exactly when a cleanup cron would stop, leaving retention silently unenforced. Also satisfies the no-unattended-deletion constraint structurally.

next_steps: wp-contracts first — it fixes the manifest and alert-envelope shapes every other package codes against.
wp-settings next; wp-backup-cli, wp-health-alerts and wp-restore-cli can then run in parallel.
Treat the round-trip restore test as the acceptance signal: a scheduled job is not evidence of a backup.

relevant_files.description: approved proposal, Approach C selected at Gate 1
